shloka_text: अस्यास्तीरे तु पूर्वोक्तः पर्वतो धातुमण्डितः। ऋष्यमूक इति ख्यातः पुण्यः पुष्पितपादपः।।3.75.25।।
translation: पूर्वोक्तः referred  earlier, धातुमण्डितः adorned with minerals, पुण्यः sacred, पुष्पितपादपः having trees with flowers in bloom, ऋष्यमूकः इति Rishyamuka by name, ख्यातः famous, पर्वतः mountain, अस्याः its, तीरे on the bank.
explanation: The famous mount, sacred Rishyamuka is situated on the bank of Pampa full of blossoming trees.
hindi: अनुवाद श्लोक 75.16 के साथ दिखाया गया है

shloka_text: हरेः ऋक्षरजोनाम्नः पुत्रस्तस्य महात्मनः। अध्यास्ते तं महावीर्यस्सुग्रीव इति विश्रुतः।।3.75.26।।
translation: ऋक्षरजोनाम्नः of Riksharaja by name, महात्मनः of the great soul, तस्य his, हरेः Sun's, पुत्रः son, महावीर्यः mighty, सुग्रीवः इति known as Sugriva, विश्रुतः very wellknown, तम् him, अध्यास्ते is residing.
explanation: The mighty son of Riksharaja, the great soul, the Sun whose son was the wellknown Sugriva, resides on this mountain.
hindi: ऋक्षरजा नामक महात्मा वानर के पुत्र कपिश्रेष्ठ महापराक्रमी सुग्रीव वहीं निवास करते थे

shloka_text: सुग्रीवमभिगच्छ त्वं वानरेन्द्रं नरर्षभ। इत्युवाच पुनर्वाक्यं लक्ष्मणं सत्यविक्रमम्।।3.75.27।।
translation: नरर्षभ best among men, त्वम् you, वानरेन्द्रम् to the lord of monkeys, सुग्रीवम् to Sugriva, अभिगच्छ approach, पुनः again, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, इति this, उवाच said.
explanation: Rama said to Lakshmana, the best of men, who had truth as his strength, Go to Sugriva, lord of the monkeys.
hindi: उस समय सत्यपराक्रमी श्रीराम ने पुनः लक्ष्मण से कहा—’नरश्रेष्ठ लक्ष्मण! तुम वानरराज सुग्रीव के पास चलो, मैं सीता के बिना कैसे जीवित रह सकता हूँ

shloka_text: राज्यभ्रष्टेन दीनेन तस्यामासक्तचेतसा। कथं मया विना शक्यं सीतां लक्ष्मण जीवितुम्।।3.75.28।।
translation: लक्ष्मण Lakshmana, राज्यभ्रष्टेन by one dislodged from the kingdom, दीनेन by a pathetic one, तस्याम् in her, आसक्तचेतसा attached to her, मया by me, सीतां विना without Sita, जीवितुम् to live, कथम् how, शक्यम् is it possible?
explanation: O Lakshmana, deprived of the kingdom I have become a destitute. With my heart attached to Sita how can I live without her ?
hindi: अनुवाद श्लोक 75.27 के साथ दिखाया गया है

shloka_text: इत्येवमुक्त्वा मदनाभिपीडितः स लक्ष्मणं वाक्यमनन्यचेतसम्। विवेश पम्पां नलिनीं मनोरमां रघूत्तमश्शोकविषादयन्त्रितः।।3.75.29।।
translation: मदनाभिपीडितः oppressed by love, सः रघूत्तमः that best of the Raghus, अनन्यचेतसम् without fixing his heart anywhere else, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, इत्येवम् in this way, वाक्यम् words, उक्त्वा having said, शोकविषाद tears of sorrow, यन्त्रितः afflicted, मनोरमाम् delightful, पम्पां नलिनीं a lotus tank Pampa, विवेश entered.
explanation: Having said these words to Lakshmana who was listening to him with undivided attention, Rama, the best of the Raghus, oppressed by love and afflicted by tears of grief entered Pampa, the delightful lotuslake.
hindi: ऐसा कहकर सीता के दर्शन की कामना से पीड़ित तथा उनके प्रति अनन्य अनुराग रखने वाले श्रीराम उस महान् शोक को प्रकट करते हुए उस मनोरम पुष्करिणी पम्पा में उतरे

shloka_text: ततो महद्वर्त्म सुदूरसङ्क्रमं क्रमेण गत्वा प्रविलोकयन्वनम्। ददर्श पम्पां शुभदर्शकाननामनेकनानाविधपक्षिजालकाम्।।3.75.30।।
translation: ततः then, सुदूरसङ्क्रमम् extending to a distance, महत् great, वर्त्म path, क्रमेण gradually, गत्वा after going, वनम् forest, प्रविलोकयन् while observing, शुभदर्शकाननाम् surrounded by  beautiful forests, अनेकनानाविधपक्षिजालकाम् many varieties of birds, पम्पाम् Pampa, ददर्श saw.
explanation: Thereafter, going slowly to a distance, Rama and Lakshmana saw Pampa surrounded by beautiful forests full of many varieties of birds. इत्यार्ष श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीय आदिकाव्ये अरण्यकाण्डे पञ्चसप्ततिमस्सर्गः।। Thus ends the seventyfifth sarga of Aranyakanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
hindi: वन की शोभा देखते हुए क्रमशः वहाँ जाकर लक्ष्मणसहित श्रीराम ने पम्पा को देखा। उसके समीपवर्ती कानन बड़े सुन्दर और दर्शनीय थे। अनेक प्रकार के झुंड-के-झुंड पक्षी वहाँ सब ओर भरे हुए थे। भाईसहित श्रीरघुनाथजी ने पम्पा के जल में प्रवेश किया

shloka_text: प्रवेशितायां सीतायां लङ्कां प्रति पितामहः। तदा प्रोवाच देवेन्द्र परितुष्टं शतक्रतुम् ।।3.56.1.1।।
transliteration: praveśitāyāṃ sītāyāṃ laṅkāṃ prati pitāmahaḥ। tadā provāca devendra parituṣṭaṃ śatakratum॥
explanation: When Sita had been brought into Lanka, the Grandsire Brahma then spoke thus to the well-pleased Indra, lord of a hundred sacrifices.
comments: This chapter fits well with the surrounding narrative and is of good quality. It is published with a translation in some manuscript editions too, but classical Sanskrit commentaries such as the Tilaka are not available for it; for this reason, some scholars consider it an interpolation. Since it is useful, it is published here as well, along with its translation. -- By Brahma's command, Indra, king of the gods, goes to Lanka together with the goddess Nidra (Sleep), offers Sita a portion of divine kheer, and returns after taking leave of her.

shloka_text: त्रैलोक्यस्य हितार्थाय रक्षसामहिताय च। लङ्कां प्रवेशिता सीता रावणेन दुरात्मना ।।3.56.1.2।।
transliteration: trailokyasya hitārthāya rakṣasām ahitāya ca। laṅkāṃ praveśitā sītā rāvaṇena durātmanā॥
explanation: “O king of the gods, for the welfare of the three worlds and for the destruction of the rakshasas, the evil-souled Ravana has brought Sita into Lanka.

shloka_text: पतिव्रता महाभागा नित्यं चैव सुखैधिता। अपश्यन्ती च भर्तारं पश्यन्ती राक्षसीजनम् । राक्षसीभिः परिवृता भर्तृदर्शनलालसा ।।3.56.1.3।।
transliteration: pativratā mahābhāgā nityaṃ caiva sukhaidhitā। apaśyantī ca bhartāraṃ paśyantī rākṣasī janam॥ rākṣasībhiḥ parivṛtā bhartṛdarśanalālasā।
explanation: The illustrious and devoted wife Janaki, who had always lived happily, now finds herself deprived of the sight of her husband and sees only rakshasa-women before her; surrounded by rakshasa-women, she yearns intensely for the sight of her lord.

shloka_text: निविष्टा हि पुरी लङ्का तीरे नदनदीपतेः । कथं ज्ञास्यति तां रामस्तत्रस्थां तामनिन्दिताम् ।।3.56.1.4।।
transliteration: niviṣṭā hi purī laṅkā tīre nadanadīpateḥ॥ kathaṃ jñāsyati tāṃ rāmas tatrasthāṃ tām aninditām।
explanation: The city of Lanka is situated on the shore of the ocean; how then will Rama come to know that the blameless Sita is held there?

shloka_text: दुःखं संचिन्तयन्ती सा बहुशः परिदुर्लभा ।।3.56.1.5।।
transliteration: duḥkhaṃ saṃcintayantī sā bahuśaḥ paridurlabhā॥
explanation: Sunk in grief and lost in many anxious thoughts, she has become extremely hard to find.

shloka_text: प्राणयात्रामकुर्वाणा प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्यत्यसंशयम्। स भूयः संशयो जातः सीतायाः प्राणसंक्षये ।।3.56.1.6।।
transliteration: prāṇayātrām akurvāṇā prāṇāṃs tyakṣyaty asaṃśayam। sa bhūyaḥ saṃśayo jātaḥ sītāyāḥ prāṇasaṃkṣaye॥
explanation: Taking no sustenance to keep herself alive, she will surely give up her life; and should Sita's life come to an end, our purpose would once again fall into the same doubt as before.

shloka_text: स त्वं शीघ्रमितो गत्वा सीतां पश्य शुभाननाम्। प्रविश्य नगरी लङ्कां प्रयच्छ हविरुत्तमम् ।।3.56.1.7।।
transliteration: sa tvaṃ śīghram ito gatvā sītāṃ paśya śubhānanām। praviśya nagarīṃ laṅkāṃ prayaccha havir uttamam॥
explanation: Therefore, go quickly from here, enter the city of Lanka, see the fair-faced Sita, and give her this excellent offering.”

shloka_text: एवमुक्तोऽथ देवेन्द्रः पुरीं रावणपालिताम्। आगच्छन्निद्रया सार्धं भगवान् पाकशासनः ।।3.56.1.8।।
transliteration: evam ukto 'tha devendraḥ purīṃ rāvaṇapālitām। āgacchan nidrayā sārdhaṃ bhagavān pākaśāsanaḥ॥
explanation: Thus addressed, the illustrious Indra, chastiser of Paka, then came, together with Nidra, the goddess of Sleep, to the city ruled by Ravana.

shloka_text: निद्रां चोवाच गच्छ त्वं राक्षसान् सम्प्रमोहय। सा तथोक्ता मघवता देवी परमहर्षिता । देवकार्यार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं प्रामोहयत राक्षसान् ।।3.56.1.9।।
transliteration: nidrāṃ covāca gaccha tvaṃ rākṣasān sampramohaya। sā tathoktā maghavatā devī paramaharṣitā॥ devakāryārthasiddhyarthaṃ prāmohayata rākṣasān।
explanation: He said to Nidra, “Go and cast the rakshasas into deep sleep.” Thus commanded by Indra, the goddess was greatly delighted, and to accomplish the purpose of the gods, she cast the rakshasas into a deep, bewildering sleep.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे देवः सहस्राक्षः शचीपतिः । आससाद वनस्थां तां वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् ।।3.56.1.10।।
transliteration: etasminn antare devaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ śacīpatiḥ॥ āsasāda vanasthāṃ tāṃ vacanaṃ cedam abravīt।
explanation: Meanwhile, the thousand-eyed god, Shachi's lord, approached her as she sat in the grove, and spoke to her these words:

shloka_text: देवराजोऽस्मि भद्रं ते इह चास्मि शुचिस्मिते ।।3.56.1.11।।
transliteration: devarājo 'smi bhadraṃ te iha cāsmi śucismite॥
explanation: “I am the king of the gods; may all be well with you. I have come here, O you of the pure smile.

shloka_text: अहं त्वां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं राघवस्य महात्मनः। साहाय्यं कल्पयिष्यामि मा शुचो जनकात्मजे ।।3.56.1.12।।
transliteration: ahaṃ tvāṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ rāghavasya mahātmanaḥ। sāhāyyaṃ kalpayiṣyāmi mā śuco janakātmaje॥
explanation: I shall render assistance toward the fulfilment of noble Raghava's purpose — do not grieve, O daughter of Janaka.”

shloka_text: मत्प्रसादात् समुद्रं स तरिष्यति बलैः सह। मयैवेह च राक्षस्यो मायया मोहिताः शुभे ।।3.56.1.13।।
transliteration: matprasādāt samudraṃ sa tariṣyati balaiḥ saha। mayaiveha ca rākṣasyo māyayā mohitāḥ śubhe॥
explanation: By my grace, he will cross the ocean together with his forces. And O auspicious one, it is I who have bewildered these rakshasa-women here by my power of illusion.

shloka_text: तस्मादन्नमिदं सीते हविष्यान्नमहं स्वयम्। स त्वां संगृह्य वैदेहि आगतः सह निद्रया ।।3.56.1.14।।
transliteration: tasmād annam idaṃ sīte haviṣyānnam ahaṃ svayam। sa tvāṃ saṃgṛhya vaidehi āgataḥ saha nidrayā॥
explanation: Therefore, O Sita, I myself have brought this food, this sacred offering, and have come to you, O Vaidehi, together with Nidra, having sought you out.

shloka_text: एतदत्स्यसि मद्धस्तान्न त्वां बाधिष्यते शुभे। क्षुधा तृषा च रम्भोरु वर्षाणामयुतैरपि ।।3.56.1.15।।
transliteration: etad atsyasi maddhastān na tvāṃ bādhiṣyate śubhe। kṣudhā tṛṣā ca rambhoru varṣāṇām ayutair api॥
explanation: If you eat this from my hand, O auspicious one, hunger and thirst will not trouble you even for ten thousand years.”

shloka_text: एवमुक्ता तु देवेन्द्रमुवाच परिशङ्किता। कथं जानामि देवेन्द्रं त्वामिहस्थं शचीपतिम् ।।3.56.1.16।।
transliteration: evam uktā tu devendram uvāca pariśaṅkitā। kathaṃ jānāmi devendraṃ tvām ihasthaṃ śacīpatim॥
explanation: Thus addressed, she, filled with doubt, said to Indra: “How am I to know that you, standing here, are indeed Indra, Shachi's lord?

shloka_text: देवलिङ्गानि दृष्टानि रामलक्ष्मणसंनिधौ। तानि दर्शय देवेन्द्र यदि त्वं देवराट् स्वयम् ।।3.56.1.17।।
transliteration: devaliṅgāni dṛṣṭāni rāmalakṣmaṇasaṃnidhau। tāni darśaya devendra yadi tvaṃ devarāṭ svayam॥
explanation: I have seen the marks of divinity in the presence of Rama and Lakshmana. Show me those same signs, O Indra, if you are indeed the king of the gods himself.”

shloka_text: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा तथा चक्रे शचीपतिः। पृथिवीं नास्पृशत् पद्भ्यामनिमेषेक्षणानि च ।।3.56.1.18।।
transliteration: sītāyā vacanaṃ śrutvā tathā cakre śacīpatiḥ। pṛthivīṃ nāspṛśat padbhyām animeṣekṣaṇāni ca॥
explanation: Hearing Sita's words, Shachi's lord did just that: his feet did not touch the earth, and his eyes did not blink.

shloka_text: अरजोऽम्बरधारी च न म्लानकुसुमस्तथा। तं ज्ञात्वा लक्षणैः सीता वासवं परिहर्षिता ।।3.56.1.19।।
transliteration: arajo 'mbaradhārī ca na mlānakusumas tathā। taṃ jñātvā lakṣaṇaiḥ sītā vāsavaṃ pariharṣitā॥
explanation: The garments he wore gathered no dust, and the flowers he wore did not wilt; recognizing Vasava by these signs, Sita became greatly delighted.

shloka_text: उवाच वाक्यं रुदती भगवन् राघवं प्रति। सह भ्रात्रा महाबाहुर्दिष्ट्या मे श्रुतिमागतः ।।3.56.1.20।।
transliteration: uvāca vākyaṃ rudatī bhagavan rāghavaṃ prati। saha bhrātrā mahābāhur diṣṭyā me śrutim āgataḥ॥
explanation: Weeping, she spoke these words concerning Raghava: “O Lord, by good fortune, news of the mighty-armed one, together with his brother, has reached my ears today.

shloka_text: यथा मे श्वशुरो राजा यथा च मिथिलाधिपः। तथा त्वामद्य पश्यामि सनाथो मे पतिस्त्वया ।।3.56.1.21।।
transliteration: yathā me śvaśuro rājā yathā ca mithilādhipaḥ। tathā tvām adya paśyāmi sanātho me patis tvayā॥
explanation: Just as King Dasharatha is my father-in-law, and just as the lord of Mithila is my own father, so I regard you today; through you, my husband now has a protector.

shloka_text: तवाज्ञया च देवेन्द्र पयोभूतमिदं हविः। अशिष्यामि त्वया दत्तं रघूणां कुलवर्धनम् ।।3.56.1.22।।
transliteration: tavājñayā ca devendra payobhūtam idaṃ haviḥ। aśiṣyāmi tvayā dattaṃ raghūṇāṃ kulavardhanam॥
explanation: By your command, O Indra, I shall eat this milk-offering that you have given me — may it bring increase to the line of Raghu.”

shloka_text: इन्द्रहस्ताद् गृहीत्वा तत् पायसं सा शुचिस्मिता। न्यवेदयत भत्रै सा लक्ष्मणाय च मैथिली ।।3.56.1.23।।
transliteration: indrahastād gṛhītvā tat pāyasaṃ sā śucismitā। nyavedayata bhartrai sā lakṣmaṇāya ca maithilī॥
explanation: Taking that rice-pudding from Indra's hand, Maithili of the pure smile mentally dedicated it first to her husband and to Lakshmana, and said:

shloka_text: यदि जीवति मे भर्ता सह भ्रात्रा महाबलः। इदमस्तु तयोर्भक्त्या तदाश्नात् पायसं स्वयम् ।।3.56.1.24।।
transliteration: yadi jīvati me bhartā saha bhrātrā mahābalaḥ। idam astu tayor bhaktyā tad āśnāt pāyasaṃ svayam॥
explanation: “If my mighty husband lives, together with his brother, may this be offered to the two of them with devotion.” Having said this, she herself then ate the rice-pudding.

shloka_text: इतीव तत् प्राश्य हविर्वरानना जहौ क्षधातुःखसमुन्नवं च तम्। इन्द्रात् प्रवृत्तिम् उपलभ्य जानकी काकुत्स्थयोः प्रीतमना बभूव ।।3.56.1.25।।
transliteration: itīva tat prāśya havir varānanā jahau kṣadhātuḥkhasamunnavaṃ ca tam। indrāt pravṛttim upalabhya jānakī kākutsthayoḥ prītamanā babhūva॥
explanation: Having thus partaken of that offering, the fair-faced Sita cast off the suffering born of hunger; and having received tidings of the two Kakutsthas from Indra, Janaki became joyful at heart.

shloka_text: स चापि शक्रस्त्रिदिवालयं तदा प्रीतो ययौ राघवकार्यसिद्धये। आमन्त्र्य सीतां स ततो महात्मा जगाम निद्रासहितः स्वमालयम् ।।3.56.1.26।।
transliteration: sa cāpi śakras tridivālayaṃ tadā prīto yayau rāghavakāryasiddhaye। āmantrya sītāṃ sa tato mahātmā jagāma nidrāsahitaḥ svam ālayam॥
explanation: And Shakra too, pleased, then went to his own abode in the heavens, for the accomplishment of Raghava's purpose; taking leave of Sita, the noble one went, together with Nidra, to his own dwelling.
